# Example Grocery Habits Interview Guide

**Phase 1: Diagnostic Deep Dive (Contextual Inquiry IDIs)**

Last updated: October 2026

- **Responsible:** Example Researcher (UX Research)
- **Accountable:** Example Decision Owner (Product)
- **Consulted:** Example ML Partner (Machine Learning)
- **Informed:** Example Research Leader (UX Research)

> ⚠️ **TEST ARTIFACT — generated for a mock-run / demo, not a real deliverable. Do not file or share as real research.**

| Parameter | Detail |
|-----------|--------|
| **Study Type** | In-Depth Interview (IDI) |
| **Duration** | 60 minutes — 6 / 48 / 6 warm-up / core / close split |
| **Format** | Moderated remote, Zoom with screen share |
| **Participants** | Instacart shoppers 25-45, 2+ orders per week |
| **Goal** | Understand how shoppers plan and adjust weekly grocery trips |

---

## Pre-Session Checklist

- ☐ Participant validated — screening criterion confirmed
- ☐ Device — participant on their own device, app loaded
- ☐ Recording armed · consent script ready · observers cameras-off

---

## Consent + Recording Script — READ VERBATIM

| Cue | Read aloud |
|-----|------------|
| **Open** | "Hi [name], thanks for joining. I'm [moderator], a researcher at Instacart." |
| **Purpose** | "I'm here to learn from your experience — there are no right or wrong answers." |
| **Recording** | "With your permission, I'd like to record audio and screen. Is that okay?" |
| **Control** | "About 60 minutes. You can skip any question or end at any time." |

> Wait for explicit verbal "yes" before pressing record.

---

## Phase 1 — Warm-Up & Grocery Identity

**Goal:** Build rapport and surface the participant's grocery vocabulary without priming.

**Probes to use:** Echo · Tell-me-more · Silence (count to 7) · Laddering

**Don't:** Name Instacart features before the participant does.

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Q1** | "Walk me through how you did your last grocery trip." |
| **Q2** | "What does a good grocery week look like for you?" |

---

## Phase 2 — Contextual Inquiry — CORE

This is the spine of the study. Silently tag what the participant does versus what they say they do.

**Say-Do Gap Probe:** Ground each claim in the participant's last actual trip (methodology.md §2b.2) and probe stated-vs-observed gaps non-accusatorially (§2b.4).

- ☐ **PLANNING** — how the trip is decided before it starts
- ☐ **SUBSTITUTION** — what happens when a wanted item is out of stock

### 2.1 Trip Planning

Watch for whether planning is written, mental, or improvised.

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Setup** | "Show me where you keep your grocery list, if you have one." |
| **If hesitant** | "There's no wrong way — I just want to see your real setup." |

### 2.2 In-Store Decisions

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Q5** | "Tell me about the last time an item you wanted was unavailable." |
| **Q6a** | "What did you do next?" |
| **Q6b** | "How did you decide on the replacement?" |

### 2.5 Say-Do Reconciliation

Never accuse; never imply a contradiction is wrong.

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Q12** | "Earlier you said [recall their phrasing] — how did that play out last week?" |
| **Q12 follow-up** | "What made the difference that time?" |

---

## Phase 3 — Concept Reaction

If Phase 2 ran long, cut this from three questions to two.

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Setup** | "I'm going to show you a rough idea. There are no wrong reactions." |
| **Q13** | "What's your first impression?" |
| **Q14** | "What, if anything, feels confusing here?" |

---

## Phase 4 — Wrap-Up

| # | Ask |
|---|-----|
| **Q16** | "What surprised you about your own answers today?" |
| **Q17** | "If you could change one thing about grocery shopping, what would it be?" |
| **Close** | "Thank you so much. Your incentive will arrive within three business days." |

---

## Post-Session Debrief

1. **Planning style:** ☐ Written · ☐ Mental · ☐ Improvised · ☐ Mixed
2. **Say-do gap observed:** ☐ Yes · ☐ No · ☐ Ambiguous — plus one-line rationale
3. **Most diagnostic verbatim quote:** one sentence, exact words from the participant
